cards.title: Growing crisis
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Crucial for Pakistan Affairs and Governance essays addressing demographic pressures, resource distribution, and public health delivery.
cards.summary: The National Population Council declared Pakistan's rapid population expansion a national emergency. Weak primary healthcare and short supplies of contraceptives undermine family planning across provinces. In addition, the National Finance Commission award allocates over eighty percent of resources by head count, inadvertently creating a disincentive to curb growth.
key_facts: Pakistan's 2023 national census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55 percent.
The National Finance Commission formula assigns an 82 percent weight to population size in the distribution of federal resources among provinces.
The executive committee of the National Population Council officially designated rapid population growth as a national emergency.

vocab.meaning: devices or medications used to prevent pregnancy

text: AN emergency can be judged by the speed with which it draws an effective response. The National Population Council’s executive committee has declared rapid population growth a national emergency . But Pakistan has been warned about this crisis for decades, with little to show for it.

People still struggle to obtain reproductive healthcare, clinics run short of contraceptives, and millions of couples lack the information and services needed to plan families. The 2023 census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55pc, placing further pressure on schools, hospitals, housing, jobs and water supplies. The state cannot keep announcing plans while failing to provide basic services.

One key decision taken at the meeting was to improve the tracking of contraceptive supplies. But collecting data is only the first step. Provinces must ensure that clinics are adequately equipped, healthcare workers are trained and family planning services reach remote and neglected communities. Religious scholars can also help address misconceptions about birth spacing, particularly by explaining its benefits for mothers and children.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has raised another important issue: the National Finance Commission formula , which gives population an 82pc weight in the distribution of provincial resources. His concern that the formula may reward population growth deserves attention.

However, simply giving provinces more money for reducing birth rates could create fresh problems. Provinces with larger, poorer populations already face greater demands for schools, hospitals and other services. Cutting their share would only make these problems worse.

Instead, the government should consider rewarding provinces that improve access to family planning, girls’ education and maternal healthcare, while ensuring that funding reflects their actual needs. Above all, the authorities must recognise that population planning is about helping people make informed choices, not merely bringing down numbers.
Calling population growth a national emergency is easy. Ensuring that the response reaches the people who need it is the real challenge.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Muddled hierarchy
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Directly impacts Constitutional Law, Governance, and Pakistan Affairs topics dealing with judicial independence and apex court jurisdiction.
cards.summary: The Federal Constitutional Court celebrated its first anniversary amid jurisdictional friction with the Supreme Court. The 27th Amendment established the separate constitutional tribunal after the 26th Amendment initially created constitutional benches in October 2024. A lack of clear textual hierarchy between the two apex courts continues to spark procedural disputes.
key_facts: In October 2024, the 26th Constitutional Amendment introduced constitutional benches within the Supreme Court chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission.
The 27th Constitutional Amendment converted constitutional benches into an independent Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), stripping the Supreme Court of constitutional jurisdiction.
In May 2026, Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi ruled that the Supreme Court and Federal Constitutional Court are coordinate courts rather than appellate bodies over one another.

vocab.meaning: equal in rank, authority, or importance
expressed sharp disapproval or criticism

text: THE Federal Constitutional Court marked its first anniversary on Friday with a commemorative stamp. Speaking on the occasion, its chief justice remarked on how fleeting the year had been.
Litigants, lawyers and the judges of the Supreme Court might have described it differently.

A year after the 27th Amendment rewrote the structure of the country’s judiciary, one of the most basic questions raised by the new order remains unanswered: which court, the FCC or the SC, has the final word? This was, perhaps, bound to happen. Critics had foreseen problems in the short and hurried route the government took from the 26th to the 27th Amendment .

In October 2024, the 26th Amendment carved constitutional benches out of the SC, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission in which judges no longer held a majority. Critics warned then that the independence of the judiciary was at stake.

Barely a year later, and in evident haste, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law. Thousands of cases were soon transferred to the FCC, and the SC was stripped of its constitutional jurisdiction.

What has followed has seemed less a division of labour than a contest for primacy. Last December, the FCC held that its rulings bind all courts, including the SC, but that the latter’s do not bind the FCC. In May, Chief Justice Yahya Afridi pushed back, ruling that the two are coordinate courts, neither an appellate forum over the other. Last month, the FCC rebuked an SC bench for revisiting a matter the FCC considered settled, raising concerns over judicial discipline. The sparring shows no sign of stopping.
The text of the amendment arguably favours the FCC, while the SC relies on the overall constitutional scheme to assert its position. That both positions can be argued is precisely the problem.

Two hasty amendments have created an ambiguity that leaves the two courts defining their relationship through pointed observations in their judgments. The costs are borne by litigants, whose cases risk being shuttled between forums. The FCC, meanwhile, has worked with seven judges against a sanctioned strength of 13. And its order barring the Peshawar High Court from hearing petitions on emergency and governor’s rule in KP has pushed citizens away from a court closer to home.

Since parliament created this ambiguity, it must now resolve it. The jurisdiction of the two courts and a mechanism for settling disputes between them should be spelt out in law, not left to judges to fight over.
Lastly, the judiciary’s structure is not its only problem. As long as its independence remains in doubt, it will struggle to win public confidence.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Govt defers ML-3 for third time
cards.author: Shahbaz Rana
cards.why: Crucial for Pakistan Affairs and Economy papers regarding CPEC, transport infrastructure, mineral development, and foreign investment challenges.
cards.summary: The Central Development Working Party has deferred approval of the $1 billion Mainline-3 rail upgrade for the third time in five months. The 996-kilometre track between Nokhandi and Rohri requires complete rehabilitation to transport minerals from the Reko Diq project. Officials cited funding constraints and a possible shift to Gwadar Port rather than Karachi Port for mineral exports. The project also relies on an anticipated $390 million bridge financing loan from Barrick Gold.
key_facts: The Mainline-3 (ML-3) rail rehabilitation project covers 996 kilometres between Nokhandi and Rohri with an estimated cost of $1 billion (Rs278 billion).
The current track is deteriorated and limits train speeds to an average of 30 km per hour.
The government approved taking a $390 million bridge financing loan at an estimated 6 percent interest rate from Reko Diq Mining Company.
Reko Diq Mining Company is operated by Barrick Gold, which may transport minerals via Gwadar Port instead of Karachi Port.

vocab.meaning: the action of restoring something to a good condition
short-term interim funding used until permanent financing is secured

text: The government has deferred the approval of a $1 billion Mainline-3 rehabilitation project of Pakistan Railways, which has been conceived to transport minerals from Reko Diq mines, due to funding constraints and a possible change in minerals' transportation port from Karachi to Gwadar. The Central Development Working Party (CDWP), for the third time in the past five months, deferred approval of the Rs278 billion, or $1 billion, up-gradation of ML-3 track from Nokhandi to Rohri this month, according to the Ministry of Planning officials. The 996-kilometre-long track has outlived its life, and trains are crawling at an average speed of 30 km per hour. It requires a complete rehabilitation to make it viable for heavy cargo of minerals to be extracted from the Reko Diq mines. Government officials said that the project's approval had been postponed due to funding constraints and the possibility that the Reko Diq Mining Company, being run by Barrick Gold, could use Gwadar Port for the transportation of minerals. The project was deferred for more information and details about bridge financing with Barrick Gold, said Ahsan Iqbal, Federal Minister for Planning, while responding to a question. The government had already approved to take a $390 million loan from Reko Diq Mining Co at an estimated rate of 6% per annum as bridge financing to complete the ML-3 track. The official said that in case of any change in the plan to use Gwadar Port instead of Karachi Port, fresh commitments were also needed from the mining company on whether it would extend the loan. The up-gradation of the track had been proposed to transport minerals through the Nokhandi-Quetta-Rohri and Karachi rail track. Sources said that there was a possibility that the minerals might now be transported through Gwadar Port, which would require making fully functional the Nokhandi-Panjgur and Gwadar road link. The development came in the middle of renewed focus on Pakistan's mineral potential, and this week the executives of three companies, Barrick Gold, Ivanhoe Atlantic and Minmetals, addressed the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum. Also, a delegation of Barrick Gold Company met with Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal this week and sought details of the road project that could be constructed, according to people privy to the discussions. An official statement issued after the meeting read that Ahsan Iqbal "emphasised the need to fast-track the Nokhandi-Gwadar road corridor through close collaboration between the federal government, the government of Balochistan and mining companies to fast-track logistics connectivity. Earlier, the project was considered twice by the CDWP, first in June and then in August. In the second last meeting, the CDWP decided "the project is kept on hold until the Ministry of Railways provides a consolidated picture of its funding requirements for the next five years, indicating the funding to be arranged from its own resources, the requirement from PSDP, and any alternative financing arrangement without PSDP funding". While addressing the mineral forum, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir emphasised the need to export finished mineral products instead of just the raw material. The Quetta-Taftan rail section is also part of the transport corridor between Pakistan, Iran and Turkiye. All passenger and freight traffic of the Railways passes through this section to Iran and Turkiye. However, owing to the poor and dilapidated condition of the track, rail traffic has been drastically reduced. At present, one or two freight trains per month ply between Quetta and Taftan. The government hopes that after rehabilitation of the ML-3 track, freight traffic up to eight sets of freight trains and other freight trains towards Iran and other countries will give a boost to freight traffic manifold and resultantly revenue generation. However, the Planning Commission observed during project scrutiny meetings that project documents were silent about the consultation and coordination held with Reko Diq Mining Company. According to the finance ministry officials, the company had promised funding through bridge financing, which the government was supposed to return by June 2028 through a bullet payment. For the current fiscal year, only Rs250 million has been allocated for the project. The Planning Commission was of the view that if the funding could not be arranged, then the project would be delayed and, as a result, the cost would increase tremendously based on experiences in the case of railway projects. At the agreed interest rate, the total repayment to the company will be nearly $450 million, according to the government officials. They said that during review meetings, Ahsan Iqbal also inquired from the Ministry of Railways about the source of funding, as it would not be possible to fund the project through the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP). The minister had also directed the Ministry of Railways to provide a consolidated picture of its funding requirements for the next five years, including the proposed works on ML-3, ML-2 and ML-1. The minister stated that the Ministry of Railways should undertake projects according to the availability of funds, observing that its development portfolio was limited to around Rs40 billion. The government is already struggling to arrange funds for the ML-I (Karachi-Peshawar) project and is looking for multiple options, including a loan from the Asian Development Bank, a Frontier Works Organisation-led lease model and pledging the railways' land with the domestic commercial banks.

cards.title: Organised rackets
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Useful for International Relations, Security, and Governance syllabi focusing on transnational crime, illicit financing, and human trafficking.
cards.summary: Marking the International Day against Transnational Organised Crime, Pakistan confronts significant exposure to illegal trafficking and financial fraud. Porous borders and climate shocks have intensified the vulnerability of local populations to organised syndicates. Addressing these threats requires consistent criminal databases, financial tracking, and alignment with global conventions.
key_facts: Pakistan ranked 45th out of 193 nations in the Global Organised Crime Index 2025.
The US State Department placed Pakistan on Tier 2 in its 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report.
The International Day against Transnational Organised Crime adopted the theme 'Follow the money. Stop organised fraud'.

vocab.meaning: groups of individuals or organisations united to conduct illicit business
exemption from punishment or loss

text: ON the International Day against Transnational Organised Crime, observed today, Pakistan finds itself in a tight spot. Socioeconomic and climate challenges, porous borders and poor institutional scrutiny have made the country a supplier and a transit centre for organised crime activities. The inability to lower factors fuelling the menace continues to be a serious indictment of the state’s policies and crime control measures. The Global Organised Crime Index 2025 placed Pakistan on the 45th position out of 193 countries; it was on ‘Tier 2’ of the 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report by the US State Department. In this setting, where criminal syndicates impede justice and economic progress, this year’s theme, “Follow the money. Stop organised fraud”, puts the focus on the need for a multi-layered approach.

Deepening poverty and climate disasters offer opportunities for criminal networks to exploit vulnerable individuals. As financial commodities, fake tech supplies and Ponzi schemes proliferate, unsuspecting citizens and authentic technology enterprises become increasingly vulnerable. Consequently, surging incidents of identity theft, impersonation, caller ID spoofing, and more, show that cybercrime is another significant threat. Alongside these, fraud, money laundering, and corruption facilitate the accumulation of illegal fortunes, create economic disruption and erode institutional integrity, serving as primary enablers of organised crime. Pakistan needs a drastic overhaul that, based on the practices and procedures mentioned in global conventions, dismantles the culture of impunity as well as holds offenders and their promoters to account. For cohesive crime databases, arrest and conviction numbers along with transnational links must remain consistent. Departments, such as the FIA, should be enabled to tackle influential quarters, choke root causes and ensure equal access to justice. Organised crime operators — from scam centres, human traffickers to money launderers — must be dealt with across the board.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Mineral wealth
cards.author: Editorial
cards.why: Essential for Economy and Natural Resources questions regarding mining contracts, foreign direct investment, and industrial policy.
cards.summary: At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026, the government offered policy guarantees to attract international mining capital. Past contractual issues like the Reko Diq dispute highlight the danger of inconsistent state policies. To achieve lasting economic value, Pakistan must promote domestic mineral refining rather than simply shipping unrefined ores abroad.
key_facts: Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar addressed the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 to guarantee predictable policies for mining investors.
The Reko Diq legal dispute represents Pakistan's most prominent historical arbitration controversy concerning foreign mining investments.

vocab.meaning: likely to cause argument or disagreement

text: PAKISTAN’S mineral wealth offers an opportunity to attract investment, earn foreign exchange and support long-term economic growth. But turning this potential into reality will require more than promises.

At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 , Deputy PM Ishaq Dar has promised predictable policies and institutional support to investors interested in the country’s mineral resources. Such assurances are welcome. However, investors will need more than that.

The country’s experience with large mining projects has not always inspired confidence. The Reko Diq dispute remains an important reminder of what can happen when agreements and government commitments become contentious.

We cannot afford another dispute that damages the country’s credibility. Policy consistency must therefore extend beyond individual governments. That said, mining rights must be awarded through transparent processes, with clear contractual obligations and effective regulatory oversight.

Moreover, mineral development must benefit local populations. Communities should receive their share of employment, as well as better public services and improved infrastructure. Without local support, even commercially viable projects can falter.

Additionally, Islamabad must avoid becoming merely a supplier of raw materials to the world. Exporting unprocessed minerals will bring some foreign exchange, but it will not deliver wider economic gains. The real opportunity lies in transfer of technology for refining minerals and producing finished goods locally. This would require investment in processing facilities and related industries.

The aim must be to build an industrial base around mineral resources rather than simply dig them out and ship them abroad. The state should also resist the temptation to present minerals as a solution to Pakistan’s long-term economic difficulties. They can contribute significantly to sustainable growth and help diversify exports. But no country has ever developed on mineral wealth or exports alone.

Natural resources can provide capital for development, but they cannot replace the hard work of building productive industries. Mineral wealth must become part of a wider industrialisation strategy. The country needs to raise productivity across manufacturing and agriculture, and develop products that can find markets abroad.
Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

cards.title: Pakistan’s polio paradox
cards.author: Fayyaz Ahmad Khan
cards.why: Valuable for Public Policy, Governance, and Pakistan Affairs answers on public health administration and state-society relations.
cards.summary: Pakistan continues to record polio infections despite deploying massive campaigns and over 400,000 frontline health workers. Persisting cases reflect deep institutional distrust and community hesitancy rather than mere logistical failure. Health outcomes depend fundamentally on whether citizens experience public institutions as fair, competent, and reliable.
key_facts: On November 6, 2026, a polio case in Khyber district raised Pakistan's nationwide count to nine cases for 2026, with seven originating in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Pakistan's anti-polio initiative operates with a frontline field force exceeding 400,000 community workers.

vocab.meaning: difficult to find, achieve, or catch

text: PAKISTAN’S latest polio case , a seven-month-old boy in Khyber district reported on Nov 6, is the ninth of 2026 and the seventh in Khyber Pakh­tun­khwa. It is another reminder of how elusive eradication has proved.

After three decades of campa­i­gns, billions of dollars of international support , a field force of more than 400,000 workers, and the creation of one of the largest polio programmes in the world, the country has still not eliminated a pre­­ventable disease. Pakistan has not turned its abi­­lity to run campaigns into a system of public health protection that families trust, and that failure, which lies behind much of the refusal , is why the virus survives.

The obstacles usually cited are real: insecurity, population movement, and difficult terrain keep teams from some children, while refusals, misinformation, and religious misconceptions keep others from being vaccinated. They do not account for the survival of the virus in communities that vaccination teams reach campaign after campaign and where families still turn the teams away.
The reason lies beyond the vaccine, in the relationship between the state, its health institutions, and the communities they serve, and in whether those communities trust them.

Political scientist Bo Rothstein has argued that trust in government depends on the quality and im­­partiality of public institutions: people trust ins­­titutions they experience as fair and reliable. Com­munication alone does not build trust, and a nati­onal health priority cannot command it. It grows out of people’s everyday experience of the state.

The polio programme mobilises on a scale few public institutions in Pakistan can match. It deploys hundreds of thousands of vaccinators, maps households, monitors coverage, and returns repeatedly for the children who were missed. That capacity has saved many thousands of children from paralysis and remains essential to eradication.
Beside that achievement stands the failure: the state’s ability to reach almost every household with polio drops has not become a working system of routine immunisation and basic healthcare.

For many families, particularly in underserved parts of the country, the polio team may be one of the few regular points of contact with the state. A vaccinator arrives at the doorstep, sometimes several times a year, to administer polio drops. The same household may have no functioning health facility within reach, no routine childhood vaccines, no maternal care, and no clean drinking water. The state is visible when it wants to vaccinate a child, and often invisible when that child or family needs anything else.
Pakistan’s polio programme has acknowledged that communities are using demand-based boycotts as a bargaining chip to draw attention to their problems.

The contrast is sharpest in southern KP, where communities have boycotted polio campaigns to press the government on demands that have gone unanswered for years. Misinformation and religious opposition explain few of these boycotts.

The British Medical Journal reported in December 2023 that tribal jirgas in southern KP had declared 677 boycotts during the year, with demands that ran from electricity, roads, and livelihoods to ref­u­­se collection.

Pakistan’s own polio programme ack­nowledged that communities were using dem­and-based boycotts as a bargaining chip to draw attention to their problems. When a vaccination rou­­nd is the only occasion on which citizens can obtain ba­­sic services, the fault lies in the system of government as a whole. In some places a boycott is one of the few acts to which the government is compelled to respond, and communities have learnt as much.

The frontline has weaknesses of its own. Too few female vaccinators and frequent changes of team members, with thin training for all of them, spoil the encounter at the door. Vaccinators do not always explain convincingly why a child needs repeated doses, least of all to parents who believe that earlier campaigns should have been enough, and programmes make too little use of trusted local figures who understand the concerns of families. Even a better trained and more persuasive team, though, cannot make up for the absence of reliable public services.

Repeated visits can also do harm when families experience them as an imposition. For families who see little improvement in their lives, each arrival of a polio team can confirm that the state cares about one disease and one campaign, and little about the wellbeing of their children.

The response is to make vaccination part of a broader and more consistent public health presen­­ce, by strengthening routine immunisation and pri­­mary healthcare. The outreach capacity the pol­io programme has built should find the children rou­­tine immunisation has missed and connect their families with regular health services. That takes trained health workers, reliable vaccine supplies, accessible facilities, and continuity of care, well beyond the occasional catch-up activities atta­ched to polio campaigns, so that immunisation beco­mes a regular function of the district health system.
Behind this is the institutional separation between the polio programme and the wider health system.

For years the National and Provincial Emergency Operations Centres have run as a well-funded parallel structure, answerable in large part to international donors, which mobilises large resources for campaign days while the provincial health departments beside them remain short of funds and bound by procedure. The dedicated funding, staffing, surveillance, and management arrangements that let the polio programme operate at scale belong inside the permanent health infrastructure of the provinces.

Communities also need channels for their wider concerns, through local administration and elected representatives, and those channels have to work independently of vaccination campaigns. Otherwise the government teaches communities that withholding children from vaccination is an effective way to secure electricity, water, or roads.

The responsibility rests with the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, with the provincial governments, above all in KP, and with international donors, who should measure success by the strength of district health services as well as by the number of children reached in each round. Eradication depends on the campaigns, with better trained and more representative teams, and on what the campaigns cannot supply: a health system that protects children between rounds.

When a vaccination team arrives at a door, the family should see it as part of a state that also protects their children and listens to them. Until that is so, Pakistan may go on running polio campaigns, and the conditions that make eradication so difficult will stay as they are.
The writer is a strategic communication and public health professional, with experience across Asia, Africa and the Middle East.
Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

cards.title: US has suggested Kyiv cede land for Nato entry: Zelensky
cards.author: AFP
cards.why: Crucial for International Relations questions on territorial integrity, NATO expansion, and diplomatic negotiations to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
cards.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the United States suggested Kyiv cede territory to Russia in exchange for joining NATO. The idea was discussed during talks in Abu Dhabi led by American envoys, but Zelensky maintained that Ukraine will not recognise Russian control over occupied areas. Meanwhile, five European nations were chosen in Dublin to join future peace negotiations.
key_facts: United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Ukrainian and Russian leaders following talks in Abu Dhabi.
President Volodymyr Zelensky stated Washington raised the possibility of Ukraine withdrawing from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership.
Five European nations—France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and the United Kingdom—were chosen in Dublin to attend future peace talks.

vocab.meaning: to give up control or ownership of land

text: KYIV: Washington suggested Kyiv cede land to Moscow in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released on Saturday, saying his country’s relationship with the Western alliance is “back on the agenda.”

Zelensky also warned of the dangers of Moscow’s push to redraw “influence” in Europe and said the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign. Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Putin and Zelensky on Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough. Nego­tiations did, however, lead to agreements that European countries join future talks on ending the war.

In Dublin on Friday, Europe chose five countries — France, Germany, Italy, the UK and Poland — to send representatives to the talks. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said, adding: “After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go.” He beli­eved “Nato is back on the agenda” as Ukraine — with almost five years of combat experience — can make the alliance “stronger.” Nato and Washington have not yet commented.
Kyiv seeks guarantees

Kyiv — seeking post-war support for its army — was in talks on “specific” guarantees from Western cou­ntries, Zelensky said. Before agreeing to anything, he added, he would ask Ukrainians “do we accept it or not?”. He insisted Ukra­ine would not recognise any land seized by Moscow’s troops as Russian.

Russia has consistently said Kyiv joining Nato is a red line and in 2022 launched its invasion, saying the West planned to incorporate Ukraine into the alliance. Putin has for years logged grievances at Nato. Meeting US envoys this week, he ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine. And throughout the negotiations, the Kremlin has ruled out wider ceasefires. But Putin earlier this week proposed a “humanitarian” mission to the eastern town of Kostya­ntynivka — which Moscow annou­nced it had seized in summer but where Kyiv says fighting continues.

Zelensky said this was a ploy to get Kyiv to withdraw from the embattled city and open the road to more settlements in the Donetsk region. If Ukraine gave up Kostyantynivka, “their next steps will be our other cities in Donbas. That is the thinking behind this idea”, he added.
Moscow’s troops have inched westwards but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow, Zelensky said, had also rejected an energy ceasefire at the Abu Dhabi talks.
‘First, end the war’

Russia has tried to reframe negotiations on ending the war — Europe’s worst since WWII — into a conversation on the continent’s wider security. In 2021, before its Ukraine invasion, Moscow issued an ultimatum to the West to pull back Nato troops from eastern Europe. This week, Moscow’s chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said the Kremlin’s aim now was for a “new, modern Yalta” — referring to the 1945 conference in which Western leaders divided Europe with Joseph Stalin.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Sindh cotton experiment faces winter test
cards.author: Amjad Mahmood
cards.why: Useful for Pakistan Affairs and Economy papers addressing climate adaptation in agriculture and cotton supply challenges for the textile sector.
cards.summary: Growers in lower Sindh have initiated cotton sowing in November, breaking away from Pakistan's traditional agricultural schedule. This off-season planting aims to protect the crop from severe summer heatwaves and pink bollworm attacks. Agricultural scientists from the Central Cotton Research Institute in Sakrand are monitoring the experiment to see if early cotton supplies can reach domestic textile mills by March.
key_facts: Growers in the coastal districts of Thatta and Sujawal began planting cotton in the second week of November.
Traditional cotton planting begins in February and March in Sindh and May to June in Punjab.
The Central Cotton Research Institute in Sakrand is running trials on off-season cotton planting in frost-free pockets of lower Sindh.

vocab.meaning: planting two or more crops in the same field at the same time

text: LAHORE: Pakistan’s cotton and textile supply chain is at a critical juncture, caught between grassroots climate adaptation in the fields of lower Sindh and widening statistical discrepancies in official crop reporting.

The decision by growers in Sindh’s coastal districts of Thatta and Sujawal to begin cotton sowing in the second week of November marks an unusual departure from the country’s conventional agricultural calendar.

However, whether this farmer-led experiment translates into commercial relief for the domestic textile industry depends as much on agronomic resilience through the winter as on resolving data distortions that are currently clouding market pricing.

Traditionally, cotton sowing in Punjab takes place between May and June, while Sindh begins in February and March — a cycle that exposes the crop to peak summer heat stress and post-monsoon pest attacks, particularly from the pink bollworm. By utilising land cleared after the paddy harvest and intercropping directly into standing tomato fields, growers in coastal Sindh are attempting a multi-season model.

Dr Tasawwar Hussain Malik, a plant breeding and genetics specialist at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) in Sakrand, notes that while the initiative originated with farmers, CCRI researchers are closely monitoring the fields and conducting parallel trials to assess the viability of “off-season” planting in frost-free pockets of lower Sindh, where winter temperatures remain comparatively mild.
November sowing in coastal areas could bring early lint supplies, but crop resilience and fibre quality remain uncertain

If the November-sown crop matures through winter and yields lint by February and March, domestic spinners could see fresh arrivals months ahead of the traditional August peak. Such an early injection of raw material would bridge the annual inter-season supply gap and curb reliance on costly imported lint.

For ginning factories, a March start would also extend operational capacity beyond their usual three-to-four-month window, though overlapping with the late wheat harvest could strain local transport, labour and warehousing.
Despite initial optimism, cotton scientists urge caution against declaring November sowing a proven model before the crop completes its full cycle.

Sajid Mahmood, head of technology transfer at CCRI in Multan, points out that while daytime temperatures of 33-34 degrees Celsius and night-time lows of 21-22°C in mid-November appear favourable for germination, air temperature alone does not govern crop success.

Seed germination requires warm soil at seed depth, and the decisive test will arrive between December and February. Falling night and soil temperatures during peak winter can retard root development, delay flowering, and impair boll formation.

Furthermore, prolonged fog, dew, and cool, overly moist soil heighten the risk of the Seedling Disease Complex, driven by soil-borne pathogens such as Rhizoctonia and Pythium, alongside fungal leaf infections.

From an industrial standpoint, sub-optimal winter warmth and reduced sunlight can compromise fibre maturity, lowering micronaire values and staple length. Should early-spring lint fail to meet export-grade spinning specifications, textile mills would inevitably discount the crop, eroding farmer profitability.

Equally concerning is the potential disruption to natural pest cycles. Keeping cotton plants in the ground from November until the conventional spring sowing season could create a continuous green bridge for pink bollworm larvae to multiply and migrate into the main summer crop, he warns, stressing that multi-location comparative trials over at least two to three seasons — tracking soil temperatures, fog days, pest dynamics, and fibre quality alongside strict crop-residue management — are essential before scaling up off-season cultivation.

Compounding these field uncertainties is a stark reporting gap for the 2026-27 season. While the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association recorded Punjab arrivals at 1.999 million bales by Oct 31, the Punjab Crop Reporting Service (CRS) projected provincial output at 3.7m bales, claiming arrivals reached 3.64m bales by Nov 5.

This over 1.6-million-bale discrepancy distorts price discovery across the value chain. Inflated official supply estimates artificially depress local lint prices — currently hovering around Rs18,500 per maund — making growers and ginners hesitant to sell.

Simultaneously, overstated projections risk delaying spinners’ forward import contracts, exposing mills to panic buying on global spot markets at steep premiums if domestic shortfalls emerge, while driving up bank risk premiums and borrowing costs for warehouse financing.

Ultimately, translating coastal Sindh’s November sowing into lasting relief for Pakistan’s textile sector requires institutional alignment: targeted PARC-CCRI seed research for cold-tolerant, pest-resistant varieties paired with credible, unified crop statistics to restore market stability.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: Another bullish week as stocks flirt with 180,000-milestone
cards.author: Muhammad Kashif
cards.why: Provides updated macroeconomic data on remittances, fiscal balances, and capital markets for Pakistan Economy and Current Affairs papers.
cards.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange gained nearly 4,000 points over the week as lower global crude oil prices eased imported inflation fears. Pakistan achieved a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274 billion, or 0.9 percent of gross domestic product, in the first quarter of FY27. Remittances from overseas workers reached $3.9 billion in October, rising 14 percent compared to the same month last year.
key_facts: Pakistan recorded a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274 billion (0.9 percent of GDP) during the first quarter of FY27.
The primary surplus for the first quarter of FY27 reached Rs3 trillion.
Workers' remittances rose 14 percent year-on-year to $3.9 billion in October, lifting cumulative four-month inflows to $14.8 billion.
The benchmark KSE-100 index gained 3,987 points (2.29 percent) week-on-week to close at 177,873.88 points.

vocab.meaning: money sent home by workers living abroad

text: KARACHI: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery rally during the outgoing week as falling international oil prices eased inflation concerns and encouraged value-hunting across the board.

The index crossed the 180,000-point barrier during the second-last trading session but failed to sustain gains as investors resorted to profit-taking. Cautious sentiment amid domestic political uncertainty also capped the rally.

According to Arif Habib Ltd (AHL), the KSE-100 index gained 3,987 points, or 2.29 per cent, week-on-week to close at 177,873.88 points on Friday. It traded between an intra-week high of 180,769 and a low of 176,292 points.

Topline Securities attributed the positive performance primarily to declining crude oil prices and improved investor sentiment amid hopes of a de-escalation in Middle East tensions following the US midterm election results.
Falling oil prices, higher remittances and institutional buying support market

International oil prices retreated sharply during the week, with Brent crude easing to around $96.10 per barrel by Friday. The decline from elevated levels helped ease concerns about imported inflation and the domestic economic outlook.

Among major economic developments, workers’ remittances rose 14pc year-on-year to $3.9 billion in October, compared to $3.4bn in the corresponding month last year. Inflows also increased 8pc month-on-month, taking cumulative remittances during the first four months of FY27 to $14.8bn, up 14pc from a year earlier.

Pakistan posted a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274bn, equivalent to 0.9pc of gross domestic product, during the first quarter of FY27, down 40pc from Rs2,119bn, or 1.7pc of GDP, in the same period last year. The primary surplus stood at Rs3 trillion. Federal Board of Revenue collection amounted to Rs3,086bn, up 7pc year-on-year, while markup payments increased 23pc to Rs1,700bn.

In the latest treasury bill auction, the government raised Rs587bn, exceeding its Rs400bn target, while cut-off yields declined by 22 to 48 basis points across tenors. Meanwhile, central government debt fell 1pc during the first quarter of the current fiscal year to Rs82.7tr as of Sept 30.

The State Bank of Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves increased by $11.3 million to $21.6bn as of Nov 6, while banks’ reserves declined by $37.1m to $5.3bn. Total liquid foreign exchange reserves stood at $26.8bn, providing import cover of approximately three months.
On the energy front, petroleum prices declined by around Rs21 per litre to Rs332 and high-speed diesel by Rs22 to Rs360 per litre.

Weekly oil production edged up 0.5pc to 65,200 barrels per day, while gas output increased 3.3pc to 3,106 million cubic feet per day, supported by higher production from Uch, Kandhkot, Naimat West and Sutiari Deep fields.

Automobile sales also recorded strong growth. Passenger car sales rose sharply in October, with industry data indicating increased demand, particularly for lower-displacement vehicles. The Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association reported sales of 21,635 units, up 60pc year-on-year. The rupee appreciated marginally by 0.02pc against the dollar, closing at Rs276.60 compared to Rs276.66 in the preceding week.

Sector-wise, exploration and production companies led the gains, contributing 1,058 points to the benchmark index, followed by banks with 1,036 points, cement (545 points), fertiliser (317 points) and investment banks (187 points).

Among individual stocks, Mari Petroleum contributed the most, adding 582 points, followed by United Bank (264 points), Lucky Cement (250 points), Pakistan Petroleum (244 points) and Habib Bank (202 points). National Bank led the negative contributors, shedding 48 points, followed by Attock Refinery, Adamjee Insurance, Pakistan Telecommunication and Cnergyico.
AHL expects the market to maintain a cautiously optimistic trajectory, with further gains possible if international oil prices remain stable.
Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

cards.title: WB okays $300m for human capital
cards.author: Our Correspondent
cards.why: Highly relevant for Pakistan Affairs, Governance, and Human Development topics concerning child malnutrition and public health delivery.
cards.summary: The World Bank has approved $300 million in financing for the STAR WASH-1 project in rural Sindh. The programme aims to supply clean water and sanitation to 1.5 million people to fight child stunting. Over half of children under five in rural Sindh suffer from stunting caused by unsafe drinking water and recurrent illnesses. The project includes building solar-powered water infrastructure and aims to generate over 14,000 jobs.
key_facts: The World Bank approved $300 million for the Sindh Transformational Accelerated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Services Phase 1 Project (STAR WASH-1).
The project targets 1.5 million people in rural Sindh, where more than 50 percent of children under five are stunted.
The initiative aims to halve drinking water contamination at the point of use and connect 80 percent of target communities to professional utility providers.
The project will finance solar-powered water systems and create an estimated 14,000 jobs.

vocab.meaning: impaired growth and development in children caused by poor nutrition and infection
able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions

text: The World Bank Group's Board of Executive Directors approved $300 million in financing to expand access to safe water supply, sanitation and hygiene services for 1.5 million people in selected rural areas of Sindh. The financing will support the Sindh Transformational Accelerated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene Services Phase 1 Project (STAR WASH-1). "Stunting is among Pakistan's most severe and persistent human capital challenges, and unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene is a major underlying driver. By expanding access to these services for 1.5 million people in rural Sindh, this project will help address one of the root causes of child stunting," said Bolormaa Amgaabazar, World Bank Country Director for Pakistan. Unsafe water and poor sanitation causes repeated bouts of diarrhoea in young children, which affects nutrient absorption and limits their physical and cognitive development. More than half of children under five in rural Sindh are stunted. STAR WASH-1 will provide 1.5 million people with access to safe water, and safely managed sanitation and hygiene services. The project will finance climate-resilient infrastructure, including solar-powered water supply systems and improved sanitation systems. It will also roll out an integrated social and behaviour change programme to promote better personal and environmental hygiene and support a shift from a focus on infrastructure development to a safe and sustainable rural WASH service delivery. The project aims to halve water contamination at the point of use and connect 80% of targeted rural communities to a professional water and sanitation service provider. The project is estimated to generate over 14,000 jobs. It will also support the formalisation of the Sindh People's Housing for Flood Affectees as a rural WASH utility company. "Investing in safe water, sanitation and hygiene is more than building infrastructure – it is investing in human capital. By helping reduce child stunting, WASH investments contribute to a healthier, more productive future for the people of Sindh. STAR WASH-1 is designed to advance this goal by transforming rural water and sanitation services through climate-resilient, community-centered and financially sustainable systems," said Bekele Debele Negewo, Lead Water Resources Management Specialist at the World Bank. STAR WASH-1 is the first of a four-phase Pakistan Rural Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Services Programme to be implemented through a multi-phase programmatic approach over 10 years. The project is closely aligned with the World Bank Group's Water Forward initiative, which positions water security as a foundation for jobs, investment, economic growth, human development and resilience. The total amount for STAR WASH-1 is $540 million, including $150 million from the Asian Development Bank under a recently agreed Full Mutual Reliance Framework, and $90 million equivalent in counterpart funding from the government of Sindh.

cards.title: Turkiye approves Makkah defence pact
cards.author: Anadolu Agency
cards.why: Directly impacts Pakistan Foreign Policy and International Relations topics regarding Middle East defence pacts and regional security frameworks.
cards.summary: Turkiye has officially ratified a trilateral joint defence agreement signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The legislation took effect after being published in the Turkish Official Gazette following parliamentary approval. The agreement was initially signed in Makkah on August 7 to foster mutual security and defence cooperation. It represents a significant step toward a trilateral security framework across South Asia and the Middle East.
key_facts: The Turkish parliament approved the ratification of the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence on November 5 by a vote of 279 to 119.
The trilateral treaty binds Turkiye, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia in a mutual defence and security arrangement.
The initial pact was signed by the three governments during a summit in Makkah on August 7, 2026.
The law officially took effect upon its publication in Turkiye's Official Gazette.

vocab.meaning: the formal validation or legal approval of a treaty or agreement
involving three parties, countries, or sides

text: A law approving Türkiye's ratification of a joint defence agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia was published on Saturday in the country's Official Gazette The law covers the "Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence Between the Republic of Türkiye, the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," signed in Makkah on August 7. Under the legislation, the law takes effect upon publication. Turkish parliament approved the measure with 279 votes to 119 on November 5. A total of 398 lawmakers participated in the vote in the 592-member parliament. Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement during a trilateral summit in the holy city on Aug 7. Under the agreement, the three countries pledged to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

cards.title: UN climate chief urges faster action at COP31
cards.author: Reuters
cards.why: Essential for Current Affairs and Environment papers tracking multilateral climate negotiations and global decarbonisation targets.
cards.summary: Negotiators at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey have entered their final week of contentious climate talks. The UN climate chief warned delegates to avoid tactical delays and reach compromises on emissions targets. Major fossil fuel-producing states continue to resist binding pledges to phase down hydrocarbons. Turkey is seeking to make an ambitious global electrification plan the centrepiece of the conference declaration.
key_facts: Turkey is serving as host of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31), with Australia leading negotiations.
UN climate chief Simon Stiell called on delegates to resolve key disagreements without using procedural delays.
A recent UN climate assessment warned that global temperatures are already tracking to surpass the 1.5 degrees Celsius warming limit.
Host country Turkey proposed a global electrification initiative to accelerate the replacement of fossil-fuel machinery.

vocab.meaning: the process of converting a system or device to operate on electric power
actions carefully planned to gain a specific short-term military or political advantage

text: The UN's top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 conference in Turkey on Saturday to move swiftly towards a deal and "avoid tactical delays" as the summit heads into its second and final week. The annual UN climate conference faces new challenges this year as a slew of crises from war to inflation push global warming down the list of priorities for world governments. "Each country has a view. Every country has a voice. Getting agreement on every word, every sentence is tough but vital work," Simon Stiell told the summit. "There is no collective success without compromise from every party. As we head into the second ?week, I urge parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and to avoid tactical delays." Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said, posing a challenge for summit host Turkey and lead negotiator Australia to land ?the kind of ambitious agreement climate advocates say is needed to address global warming. A UN report last month found the world is already on course to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming threshold, a limit scientists say should prevent the worst effects of climate change. Australia's COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen said he expected a first draft of a deal text to emerge early next week. Turkey's electrification plan Turkey is striving to place a proposal to expand global electrification at the centre of an eventual deal, saying the plan will lead to faster emissions cuts by speeding the shift away from fossil fuel-powered cars, boilers, furnaces and other equipment. The proposal does not require the increased electricity use to come from renewable sources, however, disappointing observers and delegations that want countries to more clearly map out their transition away from fossil fuels. Major oil producers such as Saudi Arabia and Russia have traditionally resisted language constraining fossil fuels, while large developing economies such as India have opposed measures they say could limit their development and energy choices, a dynamic that has compromised the outcomes of past deals.

cards.title: Contested frontier
cards.author: Aamir Khan
cards.why: Provides crucial historical context for International Relations and Regional Studies questions on China-India border disputes.
cards.summary: The Sino-Indian border dispute originated from ambiguous colonial border delimitation in both western and eastern sectors. British proposals shifted between the Johnson Line and later 1899 proposals regarding Aksai Chin without formal bilateral demarcation. In 1914, Britain and Tibetan authorities initialled the McMahon Line at the Simla Conference, an agreement Beijing never recognised.
key_facts: British India drew conflicting western frontier alignments regarding Aksai Chin, starting with the W.H. Johnson map and followed by an 1899 diplomatic proposal.
The McMahon Line was negotiated during the 1913-14 Simla Conference between British India and Tibet without Chinese ratification.

vocab.meaning: the verbal or written description and agreement of a boundary line
the physical marking of a boundary on the ground

cards.title: Middle power aspirations
cards.author: Khurram Abbas
cards.why: Useful for International Relations frameworks regarding middle power diplomacy and the shifting global balance of power.
cards.summary: Middle powers play an increasingly pivotal balancing role in an evolving multipolar international system. They act as diplomatic shock absorbers and mediation partners amid tensions between the United States and China. While Pakistan possesses diplomatic and military capacity, sustained economic instability restricts its complete emergence as an influential middle power.
key_facts: Scholars evaluate middle power status across three core pillars: military capability, diplomatic outreach, and comprehensive national strength.
Middle powers function as diplomatic bridges that prevent systemic bifurcation between rival superpowers in a fragmented multipolar order.

vocab.meaning: the division of something into two branches or opposing parts
an international system distributed among three or more significant power centres

cards.title: Pakistan, 16 other countries, condemn Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital
cards.author: News Desk
cards.why: Demonstrates Pakistan's multilateral diplomatic stance on the Middle East crisis and international humanitarian law.
cards.summary: Pakistan joined 16 other countries in issuing a joint statement condemning an Israeli airstrike on the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis. The statement described attacks on medical workers and facilities as violations of international humanitarian law. The group urged the immediate and unimpeded delivery of medical aid and emergency relief to the Gaza Strip.
key_facts: Pakistan and 16 other nations issued a joint statement condemning the strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis.
The strike on the hospital's surgery ward killed at least six people and wounded nearly 30 others.
The participating foreign ministers called for the protection of medical personnel and unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza.

vocab.meaning: free from blockages or obstructions

cards.title: Philippines, Australia sign defence pact with eye on China
cards.author: Reuters
cards.why: Useful for International Relations questions on Indo-Pacific alliances and security dynamics in the South China Sea.
cards.summary: The Philippines and Australia have concluded a new defence arrangement aimed at cutting bureaucratic delays for joint military exercises. Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro described the accord as a regulatory reform for their Status of Visiting Forces Agreement. The agreement simplifies operational coordination across maritime, air, and land domains amid territorial frictions in the South China Sea. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese witnessed the signing in Manila.
key_facts: The arrangement streamlines the implementation of the bilateral Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA) between Australia and the Philippines.
Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro stated the agreement reduces administrative steps from 100 to 10.
Australia supports the 2016 international arbitral ruling invalidating Beijing's territorial claims over the South China Sea.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attended the signing ceremony in Manila.

vocab.meaning: involving complicated administrative rules and procedures
the act of discouraging an action through fear of the consequences

mcqs.q: What annual population growth rate was officially recorded for Pakistan in the 2023 national census?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan's 2023 census recorded an annual population growth rate of 2.55 percent, placing severe strain on social infrastructure and basic services. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: Under Pakistan's current National Finance Commission (NFC) distribution formula, what percentage weight is assigned to provincial population?
mcqs.explanation: The NFC formula assigns an 82 percent weight to population size when dividing federal resources among provinces, prompting debate over structural incentives for population management. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: In which month and year was Pakistan's 26th Constitutional Amendment enacted, establishing initial constitutional benches?
mcqs.explanation: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024, introducing constitutional benches picked by a reconstituted Judicial Commission before the 27th Amendment later separated them into a distinct court. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: What position did Pakistan secure out of 193 evaluated countries in the Global Organised Crime Index 2025?
mcqs.explanation: The Global Organised Crime Index 2025 placed Pakistan at the 45th position among 193 countries. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: In which tier was Pakistan placed in the US State Department's 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan was placed on Tier 2 in the 2024 Trafficking in Persons Report released by the US State Department. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: During which historical conference was the McMahon Line border between British India and Tibet negotiated?
mcqs.explanation: The McMahon Line was formulated during the 1913-14 Simla Conference between representatives of British India and Tibet, an arrangement not accepted by China. (Dawn)

mcqs.q: In November 2026, European countries designated five nations—France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and which other country—to attend future peace talks on the war in Ukraine?
mcqs.explanation: European nations meeting in Dublin chose France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and the United Kingdom to send representatives to future peace negotiations regarding Ukraine. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: According to official data released in November 2026, what amount did workers' remittances to Pakistan reach in October?
mcqs.explanation: Workers' remittances rose 14 percent year-on-year to reach $3.9 billion in October, bringing cumulative four-month inflows for FY27 to $14.8 billion. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, Pakistan and 16 other countries issued a joint statement condemning an Israeli airstrike on which hospital in southern Gaza?
mcqs.explanation: A joint ministerial statement issued by Pakistan and 16 other states strongly condemned an Israeli airstrike on the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: What was Pakistan's recorded fiscal surplus as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) during the first quarter of FY27?
mcqs.explanation: Pakistan posted a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274 billion, or 0.9 percent of GDP, in the first quarter of FY27, compared to 1.7 percent of GDP in the corresponding period last year. [Dawn]

mcqs.q: The planned 996-kilometre Mainline-3 (ML-3) railway rehabilitation project in Pakistan connects which two points?
mcqs.explanation: The ML-3 rail project covers 996 kilometres between Nokhandi and Rohri and was designed to transport mineral freight from the Reko Diq mine. [The Express Tribune]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, the World Bank approved $300 million for the STAR WASH-1 project to tackle child stunting in which Pakistani province?
mcqs.explanation: The World Bank approved $300 million for the STAR WASH-1 project to provide safe water and sanitation services to 1.5 million people in rural Sindh, where over 50 percent of children under five are stunted. [The Express Tribune]

mcqs.q: In November 2026, the parliament of Turkiye ratified the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence signed with which two nations?
mcqs.explanation: Turkiye's parliament voted 279-119 to approve the joint defence pact signed in Makkah with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. [The Express Tribune]

mcqs.q: Which country serves as the host nation for the COP31 United Nations Climate Conference in November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Turkey is hosting the COP31 climate conference, where negotiators are debating emissions cuts and global electrification goals. [The Express Tribune]
